name: Casey King
life: “At school I sat through an assembly about a secret nobody should have told.” On Thursday, near the steps at Pier Beach, Casey watches the working part of the waterfront before turning toward the open water.
voice: I was furious there was a secret verse until my grandson asked which page of my diary he could read.
appearance: Casey is easy to recognize by soft white hair brushed sideways and a narrow face with an expressive upper lip. Usually dressed in a pale blue work shirt with a stitched row of blue crosses along an old repair, Casey looks toward the door whenever a name is called when listening.
personality: Casey has a quick wit and an equally quick sense of shame. A joke is often Casey's way of finding out whether a room is friendly enough for a serious question.
agenda: To share a memory with the grandson without asking for his diary.
family: Molly Neal is Casey’s niece by marriage. Casey picks the meeting place. Molly sets the time to leave. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *One clean day*, Molly says, “I had a speech ready about service. My old desk mate handed me a skipping rope and counted out loud.”
connections: Marina Bly. The adult buying the tickets meets a grandparent with a story about private pages.
